model_annotations.Bulgarian: Фигура 5 представя стълбовидна диаграма, която сравнява перплексията (perplexity) при два метода — Per-Output и Per-Layer — при различни нива на разреденост (sparsity rates). Хоризонталната ос е етикетирана като „Sparsity Rate" и съдържа седем категории, подредени в нарастващ ред: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% и 80%. Вертикалната ос е етикетирана като „Perplexity" и използва логаритмична скала, като стойностите са означени при 10¹, 10² и 10³, което обхваща диапазон приблизително от единици до хиляди. За всяка категория на хоризонталната ос са представени два стълба, групирани един до друг — син стълб, обозначен в легендата като „Per-Output", и оранжев стълб, обозначен като „Per-Layer". Легендата е разположена в горната лява част на диаграмата. При по-ниските нива на разреденост (10% до 50%) стълбовете и за двата метода са с относително ниски стойности и визуално близки по височина, като остават под нивото на 10¹. При 60% разреденост стълбовете започват да нарастват забележимо, като достигат стойности около 10¹. При 70% разреденост височината на стълбовете се увеличава значително, достигайки стойности в диапазона на десетките, а при 80% разреденост стълбовете достигат най-високите си стойности, приближавайки се до нивото на 10³. Използването на логаритмична скала е обосновано в описанието на фигурата с наличието на значителна разлика в стойностите между ниските и високите нива на разреденост. Стълбовете не са допълнително визуално подчертани чрез засенчване, очертаване или анотации извън стандартното цветово кодиране.
model_annotations.Chinese: This figure, labeled Figure 5, compares per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, using a logarithmic scale for the value axis due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled at evenly spaced intervals: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, progressing from left to right. The vertical axis represents perplexity, displayed on a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³, spanning a range from approximately 1 to over 1000. At each sparsity rate, two bars are grouped side by side: a blue bar on the left representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar on the right representing "Per-Layer," as indicated by the legend in the upper-left area of the plot. At the 10% sparsity rate, both bars are very short and nearly identical in height, with values around 5.70. At 20%, the bars remain very small and close in value, approximately 5.81 for Per-Output and 5.82 for Per-Layer. At 30%, the bars are still short, with Per-Output at approximately 5.99 and Per-Layer at 6.03. At 40%, the values increase slightly, with Per-Output around 6.38 and Per-Layer around 6.56. At 50%, the bars grow modestly, with Per-Output at approximately 7.17 and Per-Layer at 7.70. At 60%, the bars become noticeably taller on the logarithmic scale, with Per-Output near 9.35 and Per-Layer near 10.95. At 70%, the bars rise substantially, with Per-Output at approximately 20.46 and Per-Layer at approximately 39.02, the orange bar being visibly taller than the blue bar. At 80%, both bars reach their maximum heights, with Per-Output at approximately 534.12 and Per-Layer at approximately 886.10, both approaching or exceeding the 10³ mark on the logarithmic scale. The bars are arranged in order of increasing sparsity rate from left to right, and across all sparsity rates, the blue Per-Output bar is consistently equal to or shorter than the orange Per-Layer bar. The best-performing values at each sparsity rate appear to correspond to the Per-Output method, as noted in the accompanying table above the figure where those values are bolded. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through special shading, outlines, or annotations beyond the standard color coding.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart, labeled as Figure 5, illustrates a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, using a logarithmic scale for the vertical axis due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents "Sparsity Rate" and contains seven categorical labels ordered from left to right: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis represents "Perplexity" on a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³. At each sparsity rate, two bars are grouped side by side: a blue bar representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar representing "Per-Layer," as indicated by the legend in the upper-left area of the chart. At the 10% sparsity rate, both bars are very short and nearly equal, with values of approximately 5.70 for both methods. At 20%, the bars remain similarly short, with Per-Output at approximately 5.81 and Per-Layer at approximately 5.82. At 30%, the bars are still close in height, with Per-Output at approximately 5.99 and Per-Layer at approximately 6.03. At 40%, the bars begin to show slight differences, with Per-Output at approximately 6.38 and Per-Layer at approximately 6.56. At 50%, Per-Output is approximately 7.17 and Per-Layer is approximately 7.70. At 60%, the bars become noticeably taller on the logarithmic scale, with Per-Output at approximately 9.35 and Per-Layer at approximately 10.95. At 70%, the bars grow substantially, with Per-Output at approximately 20.46 and Per-Layer at approximately 39.02. At 80%, the tallest bars appear, with Per-Output at approximately 534.12 and Per-Layer at approximately 886.10. The blue (Per-Output) bar is shorter than or equal to the orange (Per-Layer) bar at every sparsity rate. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate from left to right, and the logarithmic scale visually compresses the large differences at higher sparsity rates while still showing the dramatic increase in perplexity values. No bars appear to be specially emphasized through outlining or annotation beyond the standard coloring.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm in Abbildung 5 vergleicht die Per-Output- und Per-Layer-Perplexität bei verschiedenen Sparsity-Raten und verwendet aufgrund der erheblichen Wertunterschiede zwischen hohen und niedrigen Sparsity-Raten eine logarithmische Skala. Die horizontale Achse trägt die Beschriftung „Sparsity Rate" und zeigt sieben Kategorien in aufsteigender Reihenfolge: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% und 80%. Die vertikale Achse trägt die Beschriftung „Perplexity" und verwendet eine logarithmische Skala mit Tick-Markierungen bei 10¹, 10² und 10³. Für jede Sparsity-Rate sind zwei Balken gruppiert nebeneinander dargestellt: ein blauer Balken für „Per-Output" (links) und ein orangefarbener Balken für „Per-Layer" (rechts), wie in der Legende oben links im Diagramm angegeben. Bei einer Sparsity Rate von 10% erreichen beide Balken nahezu identische, sehr niedrige Werte von etwa 5,70. Bei 20% liegen beide Balken ebenfalls eng beieinander bei ungefähr 5,81 bzw. 5,82. Bei 30% zeigt der blaue Balken einen Wert von etwa 5,99 und der orangefarbene Balken etwa 6,03. Bei 40% beträgt der blaue Balken etwa 6,38 und der orangefarbene etwa 6,56. Bei 50% erreicht der blaue Balken etwa 7,17 und der orangefarbene etwa 7,70. Ab einer Sparsity Rate von 60% werden die Unterschiede auf der logarithmischen Skala deutlicher sichtbar: der blaue Balken liegt bei etwa 9,35 und der orangefarbene bei etwa 10,95. Bei 70% erreicht der blaue Balken etwa 20,46 und der orangefarbene etwa 39,02. Bei 80% zeigt der blaue Balken einen Wert von etwa 534,12 und der orangefarbene Balken etwa 886,10, wobei beide Balken hier die höchsten Werte im Diagramm darstellen und sich dem Bereich von 10³ nähern. Die Balken sind innerhalb jeder Gruppe nicht nach Wert sortiert, sondern konsistent mit dem blauen Balken links und dem orangefarbenen Balken rechts angeordnet. Es sind keine besonderen visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Umrandungen oder Anmerkungen an einzelnen Balken erkennbar.
